checks.label: The integral is interpreted as the area under the pV curve: on every screen with bars, each bar drawn is its pressure times its change in volume, the work total drawn is the sum of those bars, and with many thousands of bars that sum is the area under the curve

The area under the curve given by pVⁿ = C: the rule (p₁V₁ − p₂V₂) ÷ (n − 1) equals the reverse power rule’s area at every n from 1.1 to 2 and every end volume from 0.15 to 0.4 m³, and on the rule screen the 100 bars drawn agree with it to within 0.01 kJ

A polytropic process is one in which pVⁿ is constant: along every curve drawn, pressure times volume to the power n stays at its C, and each end pressure the screens give follows from it (100, 400, 100, 800, 100 and 125 kPa)

The area of the pV diagram represents the work done: on the steady screens the rectangle under the flat line, pressure times change in volume, is the total drawn, 200 × 0.2 = 40 kJ and 300 × 0.1 = 30 kJ

Determines the area of an indicator card using the mid-ordinate rule: each bar is read at its middle, and under pV² = 4 the totals drawn go 19.82 kJ for four bars, 19.95 kJ for eight and 20.00 kJ for a hundred, rising with every extra bar towards 20 kJ

We cannot set n = −1 in the fraction 1/(n + 1): the reverse power rule has no answer for the power −1, which pVⁿ = C gives at n = 1, so the n slider stops at 1.1; at every n it allows, V¹⁻ⁿ ÷ (1 − n), differentiated by its slope worked out from the rule, gives back V⁻ⁿ

Work done by the gas is positive for expansion and negative for compression: the switch runs the same curve either way, every squeezing bar hatched with a minus width and running back along the lower lane, the total −20 kJ by the rule against +20 kJ; every expansion here gives plus and every squeeze minus

The work done on the system equals the final pressure times the final volume minus the initial pressure times the initial volume, divided by n − 1: the big expansion’s −72 kJ answer is that form, the same size as the gas’s own 72 kJ with the sign turned round

A rectangle with the same area over the same change in volume has a height of its area divided by its length along the volume axis: 20 kJ ÷ 0.1 m³ = 200 kPa on the mean effective pressure screen, not the ends’ average of 250 kPa, and 80 kJ ÷ 0.3 m³ = 267 kPa in the puzzle after it
The piston sits right above its volume on the diagram: on every screen, at every moment of each demonstration, the piston’s face is at the same volume as the moving dot
Every puzzle offers three different answers and accepts only the right one; each answer’s number is the value its slip gives, rounded as shown

Before Check no puzzle gives its verdict: nothing red, the working ends in a question mark and the total reads ? (or the work the question gives); a picked answer only marks its own value; a right answer fills in with nothing red; every wrong answer shows its slip in red
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 5 s of its screen opening, and every pick’s or answer’s motion within 1.3 s
